title: Regularization: Dropout, Weight Decay, Early Stopping
overview: Deep networks can memorize training data. Regularization techniques constrain the model or training procedure so it generalizes better to unseen data.
objectives: Use early stopping with a validation set

method.title: Weight decay
method.body: Penalizes large weights (L2), pulling the solution toward simpler functions.

method.title: Dropout
method.body: Randomly zeroes activations during training and rescales the rest, discouraging co-adapted units; it is disabled at inference.

method.title: Early stopping
method.body: Stop training when validation loss stops improving and restore the best checkpoint.

method.title: Data augmentation
method.body: Random transforms of inputs enlarge the effective dataset and are often the strongest regularizer.

pseudocode:
# inverted dropout
mask = (rand(shape) > p) / (1 - p)
h = h * mask   # training only
# early stopping
if val < best: best = val; save(); wait = 0
else: wait += 1
if wait >= patience: stop

playground.starterCode:
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
h = np.ones((1, 10000))
p = 0.5
mask = (rng.random(h.shape) > p) / (1 - p)
out = h * mask
print("fraction zeroed:", round(float((out == 0).mean()), 2))
print("mean activation (should stay ~1):", round(float(out.mean()), 2))
val = [0.9, 0.7, 0.6, 0.62, 0.65, 0.7]
best, wait = 1e9, 0
for epoch, v in enumerate(val):
    if v < best: best, wait = v, 0
    else: wait += 1
    if wait >= 2: print("early stop at epoch", epoch); break

quiz.question: Why does inverted dropout divide by (1 - p)?
options: To keep the expected activation unchanged
